The target contains a carboxamide attached to aromatic system: .../C(=O)N... The amide is formed from carboxylic acid and amine. The retrosynthetic step would break amide to carboxylic acid and amine. So we need template that does that. Look at retro_smarts_template fields: they show transformation from product to reactants (retro). For example first entry retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'. That seems to break amide to tert-butyl ester and carboxylic acid? Not relevant.

Second entry retro_smarts_template: '[#7:5]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]>>O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]=[C:4]'. That is amide to ester? Not.

Third entry retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]/[c:6]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]/[c:6]'. Not.

Fourth entry retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])=[O;H0;D1;+0:1]>>O-C(=[O;H0;D1;+0:1])-C-C1=C-C-c2:c:c:c:c:c:2-1.[#7:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]'. This seems amide to acid plus amine? It shows product (amide) to reactants: O-C(=O)-C-... plus amine fragment. That seems plausible.

Fifth entry retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:3](-[C:4])=[O;H0;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(-O)=[O;H0;D1;+0:1].[#7:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]'. Also amide to acid (as acid chloride?) Not.

We need to apply to our molecule. Which template matches the substructure? Our molecule has amide attached to aromatic ring and also a conjugated double bond (C=C) before carbonyl. The amide is attached to an anilide (aryl amide). The amine part is an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) - actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with an NH (anilide) and also the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl? Wait SMILES: .../C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . So carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl that also has an NH (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring (anilide) and also has an H? Actually N attached to phenyl and carbonyl, plus maybe H? The SMILES "Nc3ccccc3N" indicates N attached to phenyl and also has an NH (the N at start is attached to carbonyl, then attached to phenyl which has an N substituent? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N": N attached to aromatic carbon (c3...), and that aromatic carbon has an N substituent at the end (the N after the ring). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl which also has an amino group para? So the amide nitrogen is secondary (attached to carbonyl and phenyl). The amine precursor could be an aniline (c3ccccc3N) and the acid precursor is the aliphatic carboxylic acid with the conjugated double bond (C=C/C(=O) ...). So we need to generate two precursors: the acid part (maybe "C/C=C/C(=O)O"?) and the amine part (aniline). Let's try applying template 4 (template_id? Not given but we have template_hash). Breakdown: a tolyl sulfonamide linking to phenyl which has the conjugated amide side chain. The amide is attached to phenyl with an aniline substituent. So the amide carbonyl is part of side chain attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The acid precursor would be the same phenyl ring with a carboxylic acid instead of amide: /C=C/C(=O)O attached to phenyl.
